input.quote: ARTICLE IV TERM I Subject to termination pursuant to this Agreement, the Non Exclusive license granted by Licensor to Licensee shall be for an initial period of 36 months, commencing from the acceptance date, (the "Initial Period"). The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor. Upon any breach by Licensee of any representation, warranty, covenant and/or obligation hereunder, the Licensor may immediately terminate this Agreement and prohibit the Licensee's use of any and/or all of the Licensed Technology.
input.rationale: Article IV commits us to a 36-month Initial Period (renewable for a further seven years at Licensor's option), and no provision anywhere in the Agreement gives Licensee any right to terminate for convenience. The only termination rights are Licensor-side or fault/event-based: immediate Licensor termination for any Licensee breach (p0049, p0043), mutual insolvency termination (p0132), automatic termination on a Licensee Change of Control (p0134), and Licensor termination if Licensee winds up (p0137). The complete absence of a Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is walk-away territory under the rule and fails the fallback (which still requires a Customer exit on 60-90 days' notice). Licensor itself has no convenience right, so no vendor-side deletion is needed; the redline adds a 30-day Licensee convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees and confirms no Licensor convenience right during the term. Separately noted but not flagged here: the one-sided seven-year renewal option sits with Licensor (an auto-renewal/term issue) and Article XXI requires return of materials within five days.

ops.text: IV Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, Licensee may terminate this Agreement for convenience, in whole or in part, at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Licensor, without penalty, early-termination charge or further liability, in which case Licensor shall refund to Licensee any prepaid fees (including prepaid Technical Support Services fees) covering the period after the effective date of termination. Licensor shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Initial Period or any extension thereof.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a Licensee right to terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, because the Agreement locks us into a 36-month term with no exit right. Our playbook requires a customer convenience right in any term longer than 12 months; we can discuss a 60-90 day notice period if that works better for you.
proposal.summary: Add Licensee termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund; confirm no Licensor convenience right during the term.
